items.title: SEO Test Shows It's Trivial To Rank Misinformation On Google
items.summary: An SEO experiment by Jon Goodey involved publishing a fabricated AI hallucination about a non-existent March 2026 Google Core Update in a LinkedIn newsletter, which quickly ranked on Google's first page and in AI Overviews, demonstrating how easily misinformation spreads. Independent SEOs amplified the false information by creating detailed articles with invented technical details, while major industry publications ignored it, highlighting the lack of fact-checking in search results. This underscores SEO and content marketing implications, as unverified content can gain authority through Google's algorithms, potentially misleading businesses and emphasizing the need for robust validation in AI workflows and content creation.

items.title: What’s Hot, What’s Not: AI Search Changes In Q1 2026 [Recap]
items.summary: In Q1 2026, AI search developments like Google AI Overviews reducing clicks on simple queries while boosting branded CTR by 18%, and both Google AI Mode and ChatGPT introducing ads in responses, highlight shifts in traffic and monetization. Content marketing implications emphasize creating non-replaceable 'golden knowledge' through original research and experience to drive clicks from AI summaries, as schema markup now trains LLMs for better visibility across platforms. Google updates include AI Overviews refinements and monetization expansions.

items.title: AthenaHQ vs Profound: Top AEO / GEO Tools Compared for 2026
items.summary: The article compares AthenaHQ and Profound as leading AEO and GEO platforms, emphasizing how AEO and GEO strategies optimize content for AI search engines like ChatGPT and Gemini to boost citation probability and brand visibility in generative responses, replacing traditional SEO. AthenaHQ is highlighted for its comprehensive AI platform support, business-focused analytics linking visibility to leads, unlimited scalability, and integrated workflows, outperforming Profound's limited coverage and tiered pricing. SEO and content marketing teams can leverage AEO/GEO tools through assessment, optimization, and monitoring phases to drive lead generation and competitive advantage in AI-driven search landscapes.

items.title: Lily Ray Warns: GEO Tactics Risk Destroying SEO and AI Search Visibility
items.summary: SEO expert Lily Ray warns in her Substack that implementing risky 'GEO' tactics can harm core SEO performance, which ultimately damages AI search visibility since AI relies on strong organic rankings. Glenn Gabe highlights key quotes exposing how GEO case studies often relabel proven SEO practices or mistake correlation for causation, ignoring subsequent drops in rankings. Sites chasing shiny AI tactics risk tanking both SEO and AI presence.

items.title: Easiest Way to Get Local Businesses in ChatGPT & AI Overviews: Listicles
items.summary: Local SEO specialist Noah Igler shares that listicle articles are the simplest and most effective way to get clients recommended in ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews. Having published hundreds for clients, he outlines the strategy to 'abuse' listicles for dominating local AI search citations. This tactic leverages AI's preference for structured lists to boost visibility without traditional backlinks.

items.title: Claude + SEO Will Make More Millionaires Than Crypto in 2026
items.summary: Top SEO expert Sarvesh Shrivastava boldly predicts that combining Claude AI with SEO strategies will create more business millionaires in 2026 than cryptocurrency ever did. He provides a complete prompt to paste into Claude for immediate results, quoting his detailed X article on the transformative power. This highlights the trending integration of AI tools in content marketing and SEO workflows.

items.title: Around 10k Authors Protest AI with Publication of Empty Book
items.summary: Nearly 10,000 authors published 'Don't Steal This Book,' an empty volume listing only contributors, to protest the UK government's proposed commercial research exception in copyright law favoring AI firms like Anthropic. The initiative symbolizes the void left in authors' livelihoods if AI companies can freely use copyrighted works. Free copies were distributed at the London Book Fair.

items.title: Publishers Weekly Highlights Major Book Deals for Week of March 16
items.summary: Norton acquired memoir by Fresh Air cohost Tonya Mosley, Grove Atlantic secured a buzzy debut novel from Finland, among other notable deals reported by Publishers Weekly. These acquisitions reflect active deal-making in adult and international fiction markets. Additional deals span various genres and authors.

items.title: Scholastic Signs Deal with CrunchLabs for STEM-Themed Books
items.summary: Scholastic partnered with Mark Rober's STEM brand CrunchLabs to release a line of STEM-focused books in 2026, distributed via Book Fairs and trade. The collaboration follows a licensing agreement highlighted in Publishers Weekly's March hotline. It targets young readers interested in science and engineering.

items.title: Ed Newton-Rex Announces 'Don't Steal This Book' AI Protest Publication
items.summary: Ed Newton-Rex revealed the release of 'Don't Steal This Book,' a nearly empty book signed by almost 10,000 authors protesting AI companies' use of copyrighted works amid UK copyright law changes. The book, containing only an author list, underscores potential harm to creators. 1,000 free copies were available at London Book Fair.

items.title: Scarlett Press Lands Six-Figure Pre-Empt Deal for Georgia Bowers' Books
items.summary: Simon & Schuster UK's Scarlett Press acquired two books from author Georgia Bowers in a six-figure pre-empt deal, as announced by The Bookseller. The imprint focuses on specific genres within publishing. Details shared via post with image.

items.title: Criticism of Woke Judging in SFINCS Indie Book Competition
items.summary: Susana Imaginário called out woke ideology in the SFINCS competition after a judge disqualified a sci-fi book praising its prose but rejecting it due to non-caricatured religious characters. The post quotes the original reviewer admitting personal aversion to religion affected judgment. It highlights issues with merit-based evaluations in indie publishing.

items.title: Timothée Chalamet Wears Ballerina Outfit at Oscars Following Backlash Over Ballet Remarks
items.summary: Timothée Chalamet appeared at the 2026 Oscars in a ballerina-inspired outfit shortly after receiving backlash for comments dismissing ballet and opera. The viral post captures images of his unconventional red carpet look, sparking widespread reactions and memes online. The fashion choice drew attention amid speculation on his Best Actor odds.

items.title: Oscars Faces Backlash After Cutting Off K-Pop Demon Hunters' Best Original Song Acceptance Speech
items.summary: The 2026 Oscars drew criticism for abruptly cutting off the songwriting team from K-Pop Demon Hunters during their historic Best Original Song win speech. The incident highlighted tensions around live broadcast timing and representation at the ceremony. Fans expressed frustration over the moment in a widely shared video clip.

items.title: Jessie Buckley Surprises Hollywood with Motherhood Tribute During Oscar Win
items.summary: Irish actress Jessie Buckley defied expectations at the 2026 Oscars by delivering a heartfelt speech honoring motherhood upon her Best Actress win. The post shares images and praises her rejection of prevailing Hollywood narratives in favor of family values. The moment resonated widely, contrasting with typical ceremony rhetoric.

items.title: Woke Films Keep Flopping — and Hollywood Is Finally Listening
items.summary: Hollywood is shifting as woke-themed films like Pixar's Elio and The Bride! bomb at the box office, with Elio marking Pixar's lowest opening and The Bride! losing over $90 million. Family-friendly alternatives such as Hoppers ($87M worldwide) and Nosferatu ($182M) succeed without such elements. Studios are responding by removing LGBT content from projects and prioritizing wholesome family content.

items.title: Has Hollywood Golden Boy Timothée Chalamet Lost His Shine?
items.summary: Timothée Chalamet sparked backlash after interview comments downplaying ballet and opera, prompting criticism from arts professionals who called him an 'absolute fool' for cheap shots. Online reactions included declarations of being 'done' with the actor, while opera companies responded with promotional discounts. The controversy coincided with Oscar betting odds shifting against him for Best Actor.

items.title: Elon Musk Thinks Hollywood's Biggest Night Is 'Unwatchable' All Because Someone Else Made an Idiotic Claim About the Godfather
items.summary: Elon Musk labeled the 2026 Oscars 'unwatchable' in response to a troll's X post claiming The Godfather wouldn't win today without woke changes like a transitioning protagonist. Conservative voices criticized the ceremony's celebration of Black-led films like Best Picture winner One Battle After Another as overly progressive. The article contextualizes the backlash amid industry challenges like layoffs.

items.title: The Promptory Launches First Curated AI Marketplace with Built-In AI Strategy Director
items.summary: The Promptory has introduced the first curated AI marketplace featuring hand-picked tools and an AI Solutions Director named Jordan that crafts custom AI strategies for small businesses in one conversation, free of charge. This platform simplifies AI adoption by offering vetted solutions and personalized roadmaps, targeting non-experts in small enterprises. It combines discovery, strategy, and implementation to drive business growth.

items.title: Google Expands Free AI Marketing Tool Pomelli to 170+ Countries for Small Businesses
items.summary: Google Labs expanded Pomelli, an AI marketing tool that scans websites to generate brand-matched ads, social posts, headlines, CTAs, and animated videos, now available in over 170 countries. This free resource empowers small businesses with professional marketing creatives without needing design expertise. It leverages advanced models like Nano Banana and Veo 3.1 for high-quality outputs.

items.title: Y Combinator Launches Lucent AI: Automatic Bug and UX Detection in Session Replays
items.summary: Lucent (@lucent_ai), launched by Y Combinator, uses AI to analyze session replays and identify bugs and UX issues automatically, aiding product teams at companies like Reducto and Julius. This tool reduces manual QA efforts, making it ideal for small product teams seeking scalable quality assurance. It's a meaningful new AI tool proving real value in development workflows.
